title: Penn State women's volleyball jumps in rankings following split week
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions hopped in the rankings.

Penn State clocked in at No. 16 in the weekly AVCA poll, dropping one spot from last week following a split in their West Coast series.

Unranked UCLA upset the Nittany Lions in five sets on Friday despite a strong offensive display from Kennedy Martin, who tallied a season-high of 25 kills.

After that performance, the Bruins received 118 votes, tied with Michigan State as the two squads just outside the rankings, trailing No. 25 Colorado, which earned 132 points.

The Nittany Lions quickly responded Saturday with a 3-0 sweep of USC, led by Martin's 10 kills and Alexis Stuckey's 31 Assists.

Next, the blue and white face No. 10 Oregon on Friday, which rose one spot in the recent polls. The Nittany Lions then close out their week Sunday against No.18 Indiana, which went unchanged.

MORE VOLLEYBALL COVERAGE

title: Penn State field hockey forward Ella Gaitan named Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions claimed conference honors.

Penn State forward Ella Gaitan earned Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week honors after a standout performance in the Nittany Lions 2-1 victory over No.18 Michigan on Sunday.

Gaitan scored both goals for the blue and white, recording her fourth career two-goal game and setting a new single-season high with 11 goals this season. Gaitan's offensive production helped the Nittany Lions secure a statement win in their second upset-ranked victory of the season.

Gaitan opened the scoring in this match off a penalty corner in the first quarter, with Natalie Freeman providing the assist. She struck again early in the third quarter, finishing a fast-break opportunity created with Freeman to give Penn State a two-goal lead.

Michigan scored in the fourth quarter, but the blue and white held on for the 2-1 win. The victory marked Penn State's 10th win of the season, its first double-digit win campaign since 2022 and extended its winning streak to seven games.

The junior Maryland transfer emerged as one of the team's top scoring threats, helping Penn State build momentum during a big stretch of Big Ten games.

The blue and white will look to continue its strong run when it travels to face Indiana on Friday, before taking on Iowa on Sunday.

MORE FIELD HOCKEY COVERAGE

title: 2 Penn State women's hockey players earn AHA weekly honors
author: Rafael Rivera | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State women’s hockey received recognition for two standout performances Monday Morning as sophomore defender Sophie Morrow and freshman Goalkeeper Morgan Stickney earned AHA weekly honors following the Nittany Lions' hard-fought weekend sweep of Lindenwood.

Morrow was named AHA defender of the week after recording the game-winning goal and two assists in Penn State's 5-4 victory over Lindenwood on Friday. Her game-winning goal came with just over five minutes remaining in the contest, helping the Nittany Lions secure a gritty conference win.

Stickney earned AHA rookie of the week honors after delivering her first collegiate shutout in Saturday's 3-0 victory over Lindenwood. The first-year goaltender stopped all 18 shots she faced to help the blue and white complete the weekend sweep. It'LL be interesting to see how this performance affects the ongoing goalkeeper competition between Stickney and sophomore netminder Maddy Campbell.

The two victories this past weekend strengthened Penn State's position in the AHA after coming off an upset loss to conference foe Syracuse.

Penn State will look to carry on this momentum into next series against St. Lawrence scheduled for this weekend.

MORE HOCKEY COVERAGE

title: Penn State women’s hockey drops to No. 6 in the latest USCHO Poll
author: Brady Welsh | For The Collegian
description:
Penn State fell to No. 6 in the latest USCHO poll released Monday, leaving the blue and white outside the top five for the first time since the beginning of last year. This is the second week in a row it has gone down a single spot in the rankings.

Despite strong showings in the second games of their last two series, the Nittany Lions have struggled in the first, losing to Syracuse in overtime 5-4 last weekend, and winning by that same score in their first game at home against Lindenwood Friday.

The sweep was the first shutout in the career of goaltender Morgan Stickney, who was named AHA Rookie of the Week, and a strong performance wasn’t enough for the USCHO to keep the Nittany Lions in the top five over now No. 4 Northeastern. The Huskies took then-No. 4 Quinnipiac to a shootout in game one and blew them out in a 5-1 victory in game two this weekend.

Penn State will go on the road this weekend to Canton, New York, to face St. Lawrence for two games. Puck drops are scheduled for 6 p.m. Friday and 3 p.m. Saturday.

title: Kickoff time, network announced for Purdue at Penn State
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State will have another late afternoon start.

The Nittany Lions will take on Purdue at 4:15 p.m. on Oct. 31 on Big Ten Network, the conference announced Monday.

The matchup will be alongside a game between UCLA and Nevada that's also set to begin at 4:15 p.m. on Big Ten Network.

It's the first time this season that Penn State has a 4:15 p.m. kickoff, the sixth unique time for a start in 2026.

The Nittany Lions will play on the Big Ten Network for the second time this season. Their 55-13 win over Buffalo in Week 3 was also on the conference's channel.

title: Trick or treating, fall festivities | Here’s what’s happening in the valley
author: Alli Satterfield | The Daily Collegian
description:
Correction: The previous version of this article listed John Mulaney's "Bounce Back Tour" and the Broadway show "The Wiz" as occurring on Friday, Sept. 23. The updated version has the correct dates as Thursday, Sept. 22. The Daily Collegian apologizes for this error.

As Halloween quickly approaches, fall festivities are gearing up in Happy Valley. From educational talks to line dancing and haunted trails, there’s no shortage of things to do in the State College area.

Here’s what’s happening in the valley this week.

Tuesday, Oct. 20

Reading, book signing at Webster’s Bookstore Cafe

For book lovers, here's a fall festivity that will surely excite. From 6 to 7:30 p.m., enjoy a free reading and book signing with Molly McCloy, a writer and comedian from Arizona.

McCloy will read from her memoir titled, “Nine Grudges: The Spiteful Origins of the Happiest D– on Earth,” a Quill Prose Award winner that was published by Red Hen Press last month.

Wednesday, Oct. 21

Global Bites

Penn State Global Engagement is hosting “Global Bites” in Heritage Hall in the HUB-Robeson Center from noon to 2 p.m. Wednesday. Admission is free, so just bring your appetite to this event that promises to highlight cultural traditions.

Genetics, Genomics and Genealogy: A Fruit Fly Geneticist’s Journey

This lecture from Stephen W. Shaeffer is the next addition to Penn State’s “Explorations: The Penn State Emeritus Academy Lecture Series,” a free lecture series from university faculty.

Shaeffer’s talk, which is scheduled to run from 10:30 a.m. to noon at Penn State’s Outreach Building, will cover fruit flies, DNA and Shaeffer’s work with chromosomal evolution. It's the perfect event for those looking to learn more about the pesky, little creatures that we often share our food, and homes, with.

Thursday, Oct. 22

Neverland Trick-or-Treat Trail

From 6:30 to 7:30 p.m. on Thursday, Juniper Village will transform into an interactive, Neverland themed, trick-or-treat trail.

On theme with the setting of “Peter Pan,” the childhood classic tale, families can enjoy a photo booth, games and treats as they travel through forests, coves and pirate-infested seas. Registration is not required, but you can contact the Connections Director Caitlin Rokavec with any questions.

The Brothers Comatose

The Brothers Comatose, an old-school, rock ‘n’ roll string band, will be taking the stage at The State Theatre Thursday evening. The concert is set to begin at 8 p.m., and tickets are available for purchase on State Theatre’s website.

John Mulaney

For those who are in need of a good laugh, Comedian John Mulaney will also be visiting Happy Valley this Thursday as part of his “Bounce Back Tour.” He will perform his comedy routine beginning at 7:30 p.m. in the Bryce Jordan Center.

The Wiz

This Broadway adaption of “The Wizard of Oz” is coming to Eisenhower Auditorium Thursday night. Enjoy the classic journey down yellow-brick road, with a 70s, funk-inspired twist.

Tickets are available for purchase online through Penn State’s Center for the Performing Arts, and they range in price from $57 to $89.

Friday, Oct. 23

Haunted Corn Maze

Harner Farm, which is located on the corner of W. College Road and Whitehall Ave., will transform into a spooky, corn maze destination this Friday evening. The maze runs from 7 to 10 p.m. and is sure to give you a fright.

To warm you up after your exploration of the maze, hot cocoa and apple cider will be offered along with hand-dipped ice cream, fresh produce, pick-your-own pumpkins and a fall harvest shop.

Saturday, Oct. 24

Ghostly Gallop 5k, 1 Mile Fun Run

Prepare to take on a chilling jaunt at the Ghostly Gallop 5k. Old Gregg School and Community Recreation Center is hosting the ghastly event that is sure to bring a Halloween vibe to your exercise.

Registration closes at 8:15 a.m. on race day, the 5k starts at 9 a.m. and the 1-mile fun run starts at 9:15 a.m.

Plumpkin Patch Takeover

Think you've got a knack for finding lost things? Wasson Farm’s “Plumpkin Patch Takeover” is Saturday from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. This free event invites visitors to search the patch for hidden purple pumpkins to win prizes.

Hopefully, you'll get lucky and manage to find at least one of the unusually-colored vegetables.

Bizarre Baazar

Smith and Front is putting on its “spookiest show of the year” at Talleyrand Park this Saturday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The free event promises live music and vendors in downtown Bellefonte.

If you're looking for something "spook-tacular" to attend in anticipation of Halloween, this event will not disappoint.

MercyMe

The Christian contemporary band, MercyMe, will perform live at the Bryce Jordan Center this Saturday.

With tunes meant to inspire community and remind people that they're not alone, the concert is set to begin at 7 p.m., and tickets are available for purchase through Ticketmaster.

Sunday, Oct. 25

Community Trunk or Treat

The Unitarian Universalist Fellowship of Centre County is hosting a free trunk or treat event from 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. The event will feature games, candy and crafts, and it's open to all community members.

Make sure to bring a bag to collect all of your sweet treats as you go from car to car.

Good Times Line Dancing - Beginner Night

For those who are itching to skip to the dress-up part of the fall season, throw on cowboy boots and Daisy Dukes and get out on the dance floor.

Even if you aren't versed in the right choreography, all are welcome to Arena Bar & Grill’s Good Times Line Dancing’s beginners night. From 6 to 8 p.m., you can dance the night away as you get coached on your moves.

All ages are welcome, although younger dancers should be accompanied by someone 21 or older, and admission is $5.

title: The DI Men’s Soccer Oversight Committee voted to pass a year-round schedule change. What happens next?
author: Gavin Leonard | The Daily Collegian
description:
DI NCAA Men’s Soccer could look different next year. On Oct. 7, the DI Cabinet reviewed and approved a proposal that would adjust the playing season to a year-round model, an idea previously put forward by the Division I Men’s Soccer Oversight Committee.

Since less than 75% of the cabinet approved, it will now go into a 30-day rescission period and all DI programs will vote to rescind the proposal. If two-thirds of the group vote in favor of the scheduling change, then it will take effect during the 2027-28 academic year.

Originally, the NCAA Division I men’s soccer season began in August with practices and exhibition games, and ended in December with the National Championship. Yet with this change, teams will be able to schedule up to 18 games during the fall, which begins in late August and concludes during the week before Thanksgiving, and 10 games during the spring, beginning in mid-February.

According to the NCAA, student-athlete representatives who serve on the cabinet argued that the mid-season break during the winter would allow for more “rest and recovery”, along with “reduced weekday travel”.

Nearly three months without official NCAA matches is almost unheard of among professional soccer leagues, which is more of a positive considering the college landscape is nowhere near the pros. It seems like the committee has taken an approach where they want to truly accommodate the lives of its student-athletes.

The proposed change will not extend to the women’s game, as the Division I Women’s Soccer Oversight Committee refused to consider a similar schedule change after reviewing the men’s soccer proposal. The season will remain during the fall and end in mid-December.

While the schedule change is the main cause of the proposal, its effect would be felt in the transfer portal and recruiting. If passed, student-athletes would have 15 days to notify the school of their intent to enter the transfer portal after the conclusion of the championship game in the spring. This would replace the current 45-day window and doesn’t mean that the player has to commit to a new school by that time.

Slimming down the time frame speeds up the transfer process, as roster turnaround could come much quicker in this new proposed schedule, leading to overcomplicated roster management. Coaches may need to plan for the following season before knowing which players will enter the portal, which is especially difficult for teams who reach the postseason.

From an overall team perspective, we could see teams rise and fall more frequently than in past years. Three months is more than enough time for programs to reevaluate themselves. Injuries we once viewed as “season-ending” could be a thing of the past. Teams could rejuvenate over their break, or lose the momentum they had during the first half of the season.

For the players, the change grants the ability to display their talents in two stints: A player struggling for playing time in the fall could see their role increase in the spring. Players can reshape their reputations and boost their stock within their own programs or in the eyes of scouts.

title: Big Ten roundup | UCLA remains undefeated, Ohio State tops Indiana
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
While it was a crazy week in college football with five top-10 losses, the Big Ten also produced its fair share of big moments.

UCLA earned its sixth straight victory under new coach Bob Chesney to remain the only undefeated team in the conference, while No. 4 Ohio State edged out No. 5 Indiana.

Here’s a look at what went on around the Big Ten in Week 7.

Top-five matchup

Saturday was a rematch of last year’s Big Ten championship between the Hoosiers and Buckeyes. This time, however, it was a different outcome, with Ohio State winning 19-15.

Ohio State marched into Bloomington with one loss, while Indiana was one of two undefeated teams in the conference. The Buckeyes pulled ahead with an early 3-0 lead in the first quarter and kept that three-point margin going into halftime.

Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, a Heisman Trophy frontrunner and top NFL draft prospect, was held silent for most of the game. His big moment came in the fourth quarter as he reeled in a 38-yard pass from quarterback Julian Sayin to make it a two-score game.

After the Hoosiers cut the deficit to four points with a touchdown pass from quarterback Josh Hoover to wide receiver Nick Marsh, the Buckeyes began driving down the field before Sayin was sacked and left the game due to an injury. He returned to the sidelines with a sling on his right arm, and coach Ryan Day said postgame Sayin will be out “several weeks.”

The Buckeyes held onto the victory after Indiana’s go-ahead touchdown on fourth down was ruled incomplete, with Marsh stepping out of bounds in the end zone.

UCLA remains undefeated

Chesney has had as good of a start with the Bruins as anyone could hope for, as he led them to victory against Wisconsin on Saturday, becoming the last undefeated team in the Big Ten.

UCLA was coming off of a thrilling 17-15 win against then-No. 13 Oregon where quarterback Nico Iamaleava suffered a significant knee injury. Saturday’s game was the first without him, and backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach delivered a good enough performance to come out on top.

Despite Dieffenbach throwing for one interception and zero touchdowns, running backs Anthony Woods and Wayne Knight each found the end zone while UCLA’s defense held the Badgers to just 214 total yards, winning 17-10.

The Bruins have a fairly easy schedule the rest of the season, with a top-25 matchup against USC being the main contest standing in the way of them and an undefeated season.

Big Ten nailbiters

Amidst the big matchups that took place across the conference came several close contests that wound up as one-score games.

Rutgers and Maryland, two teams that came into Saturday’s game without a Big Ten victory and combining for just three wins this season, battled it out in College Park, Maryland.

Each team scored in the first quarter, while Maryland put up 16 points in the second quarter and Rutgers scored 24 points in the second half. The Terrapins found the end zone with 2:17 left in the game and held the Scarlet Knights to a three-and-out, but failed to convert on fourth down as Rutgers held on to win, 37-30.

Then-No. 25 Northwestern was nearly upset by 2-4 Michigan State after Spartans’ quarterback Alessio Milivojevic threw for two touchdowns.

The Wildcats had to settle for three field goals, including kicker Jackson Kleather’s 34-yard attempt to win the game, 24-21.

Late Saturday night, it was the Dylan Raiola revenge game, as Raiola and Oregon faced Nebraska, his former team.

Cornhuskers’ quarterback Anthony Colandrea led the team with 164 passing yards and 38 yards on the ground, including both a passing and rushing touchdown.

The Ducks started Brock Thomas, but reverted to Raiola after Thomas threw an interception late in the third quarter. Raiola led Oregon to a 20-play drive capped off by a 4-yard passing touchdown to win 17-14 with 28 seconds left.

title: Stock up, stock down | Penn State QB Rocco Becht spirals, WR Chase Sowell has career day in Week 7
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State’s 21-18 loss to Michigan at The Big House on Saturday came with its ups and downs. After a slow first half, the teams made things interesting in the second with surges of offense and the Nittany Lions’ three costly turnovers.

Here’s whose stock rose and whose stock fell after Penn State’s fourth straight conference loss.

Stock down: Rocco Becht

Rocco Becht’s three turnovers in the second half proved critical, as each of them resulted in a Michigan touchdown drive.

He threw back-to-back interceptions in the third quarter, including one on Penn State’s first offensive play of the second half, and fumbled the football with just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter.

Becht had a solid first half despite not being able to get on the scoreboard. He once again established a deep-ball connection with wide receiver Chase Sowell and was able to work tight end Andrew Rappleyea into the game at times.

Penn State’s starting quarterback just didn’t play a complete game. Becht finished the contest 28-for-44 with 267 passing yards, a touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble.

“It’s hard to see that because it's not like he's just trying to do that,” Sowell said. “I know, obviously, he's not trying to go out there and have those plays happen, like any other guy.”

Stock up: Chase Sowell

Sowell was once again Penn State’s entire offense as wide receiver Koby Howard remains out with an undisclosed injury.

He finished the game with 151 receiving yards and 11 receptions, both career highs, and he became the third Penn State player with over 150 receiving yards since 2022. It was also his first time having double-digit receptions in a game.

Sowell caught Penn State’s lone touchdown pass late in the fourth quarter to bring the Nittany Lions within a score.

This performance comes after he was listed as “probable” on the availability report. Additionally, Sowell went down hard early in the second quarter after a 13-yard catch, saying postgame he was struck by a hip-drop tackle, causing ankle discomfort. He limped off the field and walked the pain off before returning for the next drive.

Sowell’s been Penn State’s top target since Howard’s injury, becoming the guy Becht goes to for a big play despite heavy coverage.

“It's just Chase has played really good football, to be quite honest with you, the last two weeks, and I'm really proud of what that guy has done,” Matt Campbell said.

Stock down: Run defense

While Penn State’s pass defense was rock solid, the run defense relapsed in the second half, as the Wolverines finished the game with 211 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns.

The tackling was better, and it appeared the Nittany Lions played a more physical brand of football in the first half, but Penn State gassed out later on and made it easier for Michigan to establish a more lethal ground game.

Early in the third quarter, running back Bryson Kuzdzal took his second carry of the day up the middle into the end zone for a 43-yard house call.

Then, running back Jordan Marshall found the end zone from a yard out, and backup quarterback Tommy Carr scored the game-winning touchdown on a speed option as Michigan’s offensive line opened a massive hole up the middle.

Although he didn’t score, Savion Hiter had a 41-yard carry as well and averaged 7.1 yards per carry on 11 attempts.

Stock up: Cornerbacks

Penn State’s defensive secondary had an uncharacteristically poor performance against USC. However, the pass defense got back on track in a big way against Michigan.

When the Wolverines’ offense was still struggling with starting quarterback Bryce Underwood under center, cornerbacks Zion Tracy and Josiah Zayas stepped up big with two interceptions to hold the Wolverines scoreless at halftime.

With 6:44 remaining in the half, Underwood’s pass was broken up by Jahmir Joseph, bobbled by wide receiver Andrew Marsh in the process, and landed perfectly in Tracy’s arms for the game’s first pick. Then, with under a minute to go, Zayas made a leaping one-handed interception before Penn State knelt to end the half.

The Nittany Lions limited Michigan to only 90 yards through the air.

title: Ella Gaitan leads Penn State field hockey past No. 18 Michigan, extends win streak to seven
author: Owen Lomotan I The Daily Collegian
description:
Following Penn State field hockey’s 4-3 penalty shootout win over Ohio State on Friday, the Nittany Lions looked to extend their winning streak to seven games when they hosted Michigan on Sunday.

After a defense-oriented battle with the Wolverines, the blue and white came out with a 2-1 victory over Michigan in regulation, their seventh in a row.

Entering this matchup, coach Hannah Prince knew the remaining four regular-season games were must-wins as the postseason approaches in early November.

Fortunately for Penn State, its hot streak of consecutive victories could not have come at a more crucial point of the season. Over the past few weeks, the Nittany Lions have proved they are one of the tougher teams to beat in the Big Ten, as they’ve been knocking out one conference rival after another, week in and week out.

The opening minutes of the game against the Wolverines were back and forth, with both offenses unable to put much pressure on each other’s shooting circles. However, soon after, it was junior forward Ella Gaitian, senior midfielder Natalie Freeman and the Penn State offense who dominated all the way up until the final whistle.

The Nittany Lions wasted no time converting their first penalty corner chance into points. With 11:25 remaining in the opening 15 minutes, Gaitan sent the ball through the net, giving Penn State the early lead.

The Wolverines had back-to-back chances to equalize at the midway point of the opening quarter, but to no avail as the blue and white held firm defensively within their own circle.

The second period proved to be dominated by penalty corners, and even though Michigan earned one more chance than Penn State, the Nittany Lion backline held once more, holding the lead at 1-o heading into halftime.

Just as the third quarter got underway, Gaitan wasted no time extending the Penn State advantage. This time not needing a corner to score points, the junior got deep into Michigan’s circle and converted yet another chance, giving the Nittany Lions the 2-0 lead heading into the final quarter of regulation.

However, just as it looked like Penn State would run away with the win, Michigan freshman forward Tilly Gibson brought the Wolverines back into contention with an early fourth-quarter scoring opportunity.

The Wolverines ended up getting one more chance to send the game to overtime at the 11:23 mark. A missed penalty corner shot kept Michigan from gaining more points, and after several key minutes of stellar team defense, Penn State came away with the 2-1 narrow victory.

While everyone on the Nittany Lion roster contributed in their own way, the most crucial contributor was Gaitan and her two key goals, one in transition and one off a corner.

The junior forward not only leads Penn State in total goals this season, but she has also reached a new personal career best for goals scored in a season: 11 goals for 24 points on 61 shots.

Gaitan’s performances for the Nittany Lions have been one of the main reasons why the team has been so successful during this seven-game winning streak dating back to their 2-1 win over Bucknell on Sept. 28 on the road.

So far this season, Gaitan has scored one or more goals in eight of the team’s 14 total games and will look to continue this pattern as Penn State faces its final three conference opponents ahead of the 2026 postseason in November.

What particularly stood out to Prince and her staff was the connection between Gaitan and senior midfielder Natalie Freeman, which ultimately led to the second of the two goals scored that afternoon.

“We do a lot of transitional drills, but honestly it does come down to knowing your teammates and learning your teammates, and that’s something that is a super amazing connection between the two of them,” Prince said postgame about Gaitan and Freeman. “They work so well off each other, they both just lead really creatively too, and that composure to put the second one in was awesome”

The Nittany Lions are now 4-1 in the Big Ten and 10-4 overall heading into their final three games before the conference playoffs begin on Nov. 4.

“They're doing an amazing job, and we’re not making massive changes because our philosophy is to play true to our identity, but the tweaks we are making, they’re really executing a lot of those details,” Prince said. “They’ve been excellent and super focused in film and in our game plan, and it’s been great. They want this, and I can see it in their eyes.”

title: Penn State ‘wasn’t expecting’ to see backup QB Tommy Carr against Michigan, contributing to loss
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Tony Rojas was honest when he said Penn State was surprised when Michigan elected to go with backup quarterback Tommy Carr to start the second half.

Rojas said Penn State’s gameplan revolved around starting quarterback Bryce Underwood, whose poor performance in the first half resulted in him being benched for Carr. He said the team knew who the Wolverines had in the depth chart but never considered the possibility of Kyle Whittingham making the change.

“We had a game plan and talked about the quarterbacks and who they have, but I obviously wasn't expecting that,” Rojas said. “You don't really expect that going into a game. You don't really gameplan for the second quarterback.”

It was an unexpected, although warranted change. Underwood went 5-for-11 with 43 passing yards and two interceptions by halftime, continuing his streak of inaccuracy in the pocket that’s plagued his sophomore season.

Meanwhile, Carr went 5-for-7 with 47 passing yards and rushed for 36 yards and a touchdown on four carries.

“I thought he played really well,” defensive end Caleb Bacon said. “He made some big time runs in some big time moments. He’s a good athletic guy that was able to run the ball, and he was accurate with the balls he needed to be.”

Penn State didn’t simulate Carr’s capabilities at practice with the scout team despite Underwood’s poor start to the season, with the former 5-star completing just 59.3% of his passes and having just five touchdowns and four interceptions coming into Saturday’s matchup.

The Nittany Lions had limited tape on Carr, who briefly played against UTEP in Week 3, going 2-for-2 with 23 passing yards and a touchdown, while earning 18 yards on the ground as well.

Carr was the stronger passer, which opened previously closed doors for Michigan. It was Whittingham’s gutsy decision to bench his starter, who is earning an NIL package worth $12 million, that threw Penn State off its game.

“I don't think we prepared to the extent that we were going to see him for an entire half of the game, but we definitely talked about him a little bit,” Bacon said. “We were maybe a little surprised that they made that change.”

Michigan’s offense clicked when Carr checked into the game. Penn State was forced to account for his more consistent passing, allowing the Wolverine running backs to receive less attention and break free for big gains.

“Once (Carr) got in, we knew he was a better passer,” Rojas said. “Underwood uses legs more, so we knew that the new guy wasn't going to. We saw him as a better passer.”

However, Carr got into the end zone with his legs on a speed option, where he called his own number and found a wide-open lane up the middle to the end zone. His score practically iced the game for Michigan.

Carr’s biggest strength was his ability to capitalize on his opportunities to impact the game individually. The Wolverines primarily relied on a revitalized run game to win, but when Carr was called to make a play, he didn’t disappoint.

“He came in and made the plays he needed to make,” safety Jamison Patton said. “I guess that's a credit to him for stepping up in the moment, but we still gotta be better on our end and not let those things slip.”

title: Week 7 report card | Pass rush creates no pressure, DBs have big response
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State remains winless in conference play after a close, 21-18 loss to Michigan on Saturday, giving the Wolverines their first conference win in the Kyle Whittingham era.

The Nittany Lions were competitive for most of the game, but certain aspects of their play were still inconsistent, the same as previous weeks.

Here’s how I’d grade Penn State’s offensive and defensive aspects in its loss to Michigan.

Overall: C

Coaching staff: D

Penn State’s coaching decisions made improvements from Week 6’s loss to USC, but Matt Campbell was still outcoached by Whittingham due to his move to backup quarterback Tommy Carr. It resulted in little defensive adjustments in response to Carr’s spark as he led three scoring drives.

The lack of adjustments after Michigan’s offense got going is why the grade is at a “D” in Penn State’s fourth consecutive loss.

Offense: D

The offense found consistency with moving the ball, but struggled to put points up during the game. Penn State had more first downs and yards than Michigan, but major mistakes dropped the grade down.

Pass game: C

The pass game had some good and some bad in the loss. Sowell set career highs in receptions and yards with 11 catches for 151 yards and a touchdown, but Rocco Becht’s three turnovers brought the grade down a bit.

Each of Becht’s turnovers led to touchdowns for Michigan, which ended up being all of the Wolverines’ points. His second interception was his worst, when he opted to throw it to tight end Gabe Burkle instead of pull it down and run or wait a second and have Burkle even more open down the field.

Without Sowell’s big game, the passing offense would’ve struggled,and therefore led to an overall stagnant unit searching for answers any way it could.

Run game: F

The run game continues to be borderline nonexistent for Penn State. Three running backs played, yet the longest rush was still from Becht.

The Nittany Lions had 65 rushing yards for 2.2 yards per carry as it was consistently dominated at the line of scrimmage. Despite running back Carson Hansen’s rushing touchdown, the decision to keep running the ball as much as they did keeps the grade at an “F” because it continued to have no success.

Offensive line: C

The offensive line played relatively well. The pass protection kept Becht upright for the most part, but the front five couldn’t create consistent gaps for the running backs to create momentum.

Defense: C

The defense was a tale of two halves on Saturday. In the first half, the Nittany Lions’ defensive unit kept Michigan scoreless. In the second half, they couldn’t get any stops on the turnovers en route to the loss.

Pass rush: F

The only thing more nonexistent than the running game was the pass rush.

Penn State brought very little pressure all game, allowing both Michigan quarterbacks to stand in the pocket. Carr was able to hurt the defense more because of his accuracy, but the lack of pass rush continues to be a worrying factor.

The Nittany Lions recorded zero quarterback hurries in the game, which allowed the new quarterback to settle in.

Secondary: A-

The secondary was one of the units that bailed out the pass rush. The trio of cornerbacks in Josiah Zayas, Daryus Dixson and Audavion Collins all made an impact, including a one-handed interception from Zayas to keep Michigan scoreless in the first half.

In the back end, Zion Tracy and Jamison Patton were the two main safeties and appeared as the best combination. Patton was a wrecking ball in run defense, including a third-down stop a yard short. The secondary continues to be one of the bright spots on a 3-4 Penn State squad.

Linebackers: B

The linebackers as a whole had a much better showing than it has in prior weeks. There were significantly less missed tackles, and they were a big reason for holding Michigan scoreless in the first half.

Tony Rojas remains the best player on the team, recording 12 tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. His typical counterpart, Kooper Ebel, cleaned up some of his tackling issues and was second on the team with seven.

Special teams: A

The special teams unit was very clean.

Kicker Ryan Barker made his lone field goal attempt from 24 yards out and made both of his extra point kicks.

Punter Nathan Tiyce had multiple nice punts when both teams were playing the field position game. Two of his five punts were downed at the 7-yard line, as he placed the right spin on the ball to let it sit inside the 10.

title: Penn State cross country prepares for postseason with personal bests
author: Luci Palacios | The Daily Collegian
description:
With the Big Ten Championships approaching, Penn State continued to strengthen its lineups and build momentum through a pair of invitational meets.

Across both competitions, the Nittany Lions saw strong individual performances, improvements on season-best times and opportunities for newer runners to gain experience ahead of the postseason.

Pre-National Invitational Recap

Penn State cross country continued preparing for post-season aspirations at the Pre-National Invitational in Terre Haute, Indiana. The men’s team ran the 8k and placed 20th overall out of 44 teams. The Nittany Lions competed in a field of 339 finishers, with several runners recording season-best times.

Junior Nick Sloff led Penn State, placing 33rd overall in 23:49.1. Sloff improved on his previous season-best time of 23:59.8, cutting more than 10 seconds off his mark.

Senior Brian DiCola followed closely behind, finishing 45th in 23:57.3. DiCola also recorded a season best, improving on his previous time of 24:31.3 by more than 34 seconds.

Graduate Student Ryan Watson finished 120th in 24:39.9, while sophomore Isaac Oppermann placed 183rd in 24:42.0. Oppermann narrowly improved on his season-best time of 24:44.7.

Sophomore Michael Braun finished 207th in 24:48.0, recording one of the team’s most significant improvements. Braun lowered his previous season and personal best of 25:38.2 by 50 seconds.

Another sophomore in Adam Kingston, crossed the finish line in 246th place with a time of 25:01.8. Graduate student Caiden Leen followed in 272nd, finishing in 25:13.1 and improving on his previous season best of 25:23.1.

Rounding out the Nittany Lions was junior Logan Strawser, who finished 306th in 25:35.8.

The Nittany Lions recorded multiple season-best performances, highlighted by Sloff and DiCola’s top-50 finishes and Braun’s significant personal improvement.

Princeton Invitational

The men’s and women’s Penn State cross country teams competed at the Princeton Invitational in Princeton, New Jersey. Both teams tested out some new runners as they prepared for the upcoming Big Ten Championship.

Women’s 6k

The women’s team boasted a confident second place finish out of 18 teams. The Nittany Lions competed in a field of 168 finishers and delivered a strong team performance, highlighted by a top-six finish and multiple season-best times.

Graduate student Lea Hatcher led Penn State, placing sixth overall in 21:04.7. Hatcher improved on her previous season-best of 21:28.5, cutting nearly 24 seconds.

Junior Ella White followed in 11th place, finishing in 21:12.5. White also improved on her previous season-best of 21:20.5, continuing her strong performances for the Nittany Lions.

Freshman Fancy Chepkoech made her Penn State debut, placing 22nd in 21:38.2. The performance set her season and personal bests as she made her first appearance for the blue and white.

Sophomore Lauren Stine finished 41st in 22:06.1, while freshman Ana Bondy followed closely in 43rd place in 22:08.2. Bondy improved on her previous best of 22:10.7.

Sophomore Lilah Gordon finished 80th in 22:42.4. Jane Kratz did not finish the race.

Men’s 8k

The men’s team brought out some new runners and finished 14th out of 20 teams. They raced in a field of 178 finishers, with several runners establishing or improving on their season-best times.

Freshman Thomas Rae led Penn State, placing 53rd overall in 25:23.6.

Another freshman in Matthew Gosling, followed in 76th place, crossing the finish line in 25:39.7. Gosling improved on his previous season and personal best of 25:58.4, cutting nearly 19 seconds off his mark.

Junior Tyler Rader finished 90th in 23:52.8 in his first meet of the season. Rader established his initial season and personal bests with this performance.

Finally, senior Jake Borgesi placed 112th in 26:10.8, while freshman Colin O’Donnell finished 125th in 26:26.7, setting his best time of the season so far.

Up next

Penn State cross country looks to finish out the season strong with the Big Ten Championships coming up in Madison, Wisconsin on Friday, Oct. 30.

title: Penn State QB commit Will Wood flips to Boston College

description:
Penn State lost its quarterback in the Class of 2027.

title: 'Something needs to change' | No Kings event encourages voter participation as midterms approach
author: Annabella Chaklos | The Daily Collegian
description:
Community members gathered at MLK Plaza on Saturday afternoon for the fourth wave of national “No Kings” demonstrations, pivoting from usual protests to a day of action, encouraging voter participation in the upcoming midterms election.

“No Kings: Vote Early” is a national day of activism meant to reclaim public power after repeated mass mobilizations, by focusing on “nonpartisan voter participation” and “making sure every eligible voter has a plan, knows their options and is ready to make their voice count,” according to its website.

“No Kings: Bank the Vote State College” was held by Keystone Indivisible, a local chapter of the broader Indivisible activism network, from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m., and featured speakers, singers, information on how to vote early and ended with a march to the ballot box behind the State College Municipal Building on South Allen Street.

To Christy Delafield, a Keystone Indivisible volunteer, this event, while not a typical protest, is the culmination of the last two years of public protest, especially with the Nov. 3 midterms on the horizon.

“It's not just progressives that are upset about the direction the country is going,” Delafield, 46, of Boalsburg, said. “There are Republicans, there are Independents, there are people who don't have a party affiliation, who are also really worried about the cost of living, who are worried about the war in Iran, who are worried about the Epstein files, and you know this is a time where we can come together and express our views.”

Keystone Indivisible is not Delafield’s first experience in activism and volunteering; she used to work for an organization supported by USAID, and spent time in places like Nepal and Syria during natural disasters and wars.

“One of the things that I saw over and over again was the way that people believed in what help was coming from the U.S.,” Delafield said. “Even if they disagreed with us, even if they weren't sure about us politically, they believed that USAID was there to help, and they believed that the American people at least cared. And that's really important to me. $1 spent in humanitarian aid means we don't have to spend $50 on bullets later, which I think everyone would prefer.”

Maren Larson, a local activist and one of the key organizers of this event, gave the opening remarks about how the public has responded to the Trump administration, and led the crowd in chants of “Who’s vote? Our Vote” and “Can’t steal it, can’t buy it.”

“So much went into planning this event,” Larson, 59, of State College said. “It's kind of hard because you don't see it when you just come to the event. But we've had weeks and weeks of meetings, and there are probably about 15, at least 15 people who've spent hours planning this event.”

Despite “No Kings” demonstrations frequently protesting the actions of the current presidential administration, this event was advertised as non-partisan. To Larson, voter participation and speaking out against authoritarianism are issues that all people can stand against.

“The United States was founded on its rejection of kings in 1776,” Larson said. “And I think it's ironic that people don't remember that. We should be following the Constitution, and we should be inviting everyone into this. So I think ‘No Kings' is actually nonpartisan.”

As the Justice Singers of Centre County led the crowd in song, other groups, like the Penn State student-run chapter of Indivisible, tabled and educated attendees on early voting procedures.

Cassius Henderson, the president of Indivisible at University Park, said that it is very important for young people to vote in the midterm elections because it is an opportunity to combat policy and influence that they’ve previously had little control over.

“It feels like a lot of policy and a lot of the direction of the country has been influenced by people who are a lot older than us,” Henderson, 24, of Madison, Mississippi, said. “It's a very crucial time for Gen Z to finally vote for themselves, and I just think it's a very critical time for them to make the largest impact on something in their life.”

Emily LeGault, the treasurer of the chapter and a second-year studying political science and philosophy, shared similar sentiments, saying she joined this club to educate students about how to vote and to fight the rise of authoritarianism in the country.

“I think it's really important because Gen Z has a huge social media presence, so we're seeing all the issues all across the country,” LeGault, 20, of Kennett Square, said. “I think Gen Z is going to turn out to vote because we're seeing the difference, and we have support from all generations of being like, okay, we don't like this. Something needs to change.”

At 1:45 p.m., the group marched from MLK Plaza to the municipal building to drop their filled out mail-in ballots in the ballot box, hoping to encourage others to make a plan to vote early. Afterwards, they marched back to the plaza and continued to sing until 3 p.m.

“I've been to a lot of countries where people didn't feel that their vote mattered, didn't see an opportunity to shape their government, and had to kind of live with consequences of things they didn't choose,” Delafield said. “I've met people who've had their voices silenced, I don't want to see that in my own country. And the best way to protect your right to vote, to protect your democratic rights, is to exercise them, and if people feel really strongly about this administration, one way or the other, this is the time and place to show it.”

title: Penn State field hockey upsets No. 18 Michigan in narrow win
author: Annie Alberts | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions and first-year coach Hannah Prince have made their first major statement.

Penn State secured a 2-1 win against No. 18 Michigan, resulting in its eighth victory and fourth conference win in a row. Prince’s second ranked win in Happy Valley came exactly two weeks after the first, after the Nittany Lions upset then-No. 19 Lafayette in overtime on Oct. 4.

The Nittany Lions began the match with a fiery start after their win against Ohio State a couple of days earlier.

When Cooper Cutchins was knocked to the ground by a Michigan player, the Nittany Lions struck back with the same energy. In the back-and-forth, Natalie Freeman earned a penalty corner.

Ella Gaitan rebounded the effort and then made the first contribution to the scoreboard, as Sienna Dunn and Freeman assisted the goal.

Penn State entered the second quarter with a scoreboard advantage, but it wasn’t exactly dominating the pitch yet.

Michigan had a clear opportunity to score from a penalty corner; however, the Penn State defense blocked it. When the Wolverines tried to bounce it off the rebound, netminder Aby Deverka blocked it as well.

Freeman followed up with an impressive breakaway, but her shot went too high.

“One of our big focuses was, in transition, not going on straight lines, going on angles to allow your teammate to be able to lead,” Hannah Price said. “They’ve really made good adjustments with that, even since Kent State last weekend.”

With five minutes left in the quarter, Freeman had two penalty corner shots, both rebounded by Gaitan. The Wolverines blocked both and took control of possession shortly afterward.

To conclude the half, Michigan led Penn State in shots, but penalty corner shots and saves were equal between both teams.

Right off the bat in the third quarter, Freeman and Gaitan arranged a breakaway. The duo slid through Michigan's defense, as Freeman passed the ball to Gaitan at the front of the net. Penn State’s leading offensive threat tapped it into the right corner to tick the score to a 2-0 Penn State lead.

“It comes down to knowing your teammates and learning your teammates,” Prince said. “That’s something that is a super amazing connection between the both of them (Freeman and Gaitan).”

Gaitan’s second goal of the day was her 11th of the season. The junior leads the team in goals, shots, points and shots on goal.

Within 30 seconds of the final quarter, Michigan’s Matilda Gibson scored the Wolverines' first goal, unassisted. The score was Gibson’s first goal of the season.

Michigan earned another penalty corner a few minutes later, but the Penn State defense blocked it again.

The crowd was buzzing as the game reached its final minutes. Both teams had more aggression than ever before, constantly battling for possession of the ball. Whenever one team had it, the other would snatch it back in seconds.

Michigan pulled their goalie, Hala Silverstein, for the last three minutes, hoping for another chance to tie the game, yet Penn State’s consistent aggression and will to win made that mission unsuccessful.

“Every week we do try to be creative with how we can motivate them and get them hungrier, and just keep them not being satisfied and keep building,” Prince said. “They really want this, so it makes my job easier.”

With the win, the Nittany Lions improved to 4-1 in conference play, which ties it with Indiana, as that pair trails only 5-0 undefeated Northwestern and Maryland.

Penn State faces the Hoosiers in Bloomington on Friday at 3 p.m., with a chance for its eighth straight win.

title: ‘Grow inside our walls’ | Matt Campbell emphasizes building the foundation after 4 straight losses
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — When Penn State and Michigan took the field at The Big House, it was a chance for Matt Campbell to earn his first Big Ten victory after weeks of struggle for the Nittany Lions.

Penn State was on the rise after a much-improved game against USC, building on the foundation Campbell has emphasized. While that growth was also evident against the Wolverines, it showed improvement is still needed.

“We're not where we want to be, but I do believe this group is continuing to pound away, and the way we've practiced, the way we continue to grow inside our walls, has been huge,” Campbell said postgame. “We'll see if we can keep doing it.”

The Nittany Lions had three turnovers in the second half that ultimately led to the loss. Penn State’s offense stalled out a few times, while the defense’s struggles against the run poked through.

“We got to go back to the fundamentals and the details of what wins football games,” wide receiver Chase Sowell said. “We can’t be trying to make the crazy play. We can’t be trying to make the big hit. We gotta go back to the fundamentals of what wins games and what wins team football.”

While those issues have led to four losses, there’s still five games to be played this season, and Campbell emphasized the need to make the most of each game.

“There's a lot of season left. There's a lot of football left for us to grow,” Campbell said. “My focus and sole focus is on this team, these seniors, this team continuing to lay a foundation of the way we want to play football, the style of football we want to play, and who we want to become. We have to demand a pathway forward.”

But despite Campbell stressing the importance of fighting through adversity during the preseason, Penn State hasn’t been able to get through it during the conference slate.

“You're right there to win the game, and you got to win in the margins right now for sure,” Campbell said. “We're not doing that.”

Luckily for the Nittany Lions, they’re heading into a bye week before hosting Purdue. The extra week of preparation presents an opportunity for Campbell and his team to fix those mistakes that have led to the consecutive downfalls while also building on the successes they’ve had.

The flashes of Penn State’s team, both offensively with Sowell’s 11-catch, 151 yard performance, and defensively, with two interceptions against Michigan’s Bryce Underwood, have shown what the Nittany Lions are capable of.

However, that hasn’t been the level Penn State has competed at consistently, and as a result, the team is winless in Big Ten play.

“It’s so frustrating because I know we’re right there, and I know that guys are trying with everything they got to try to get this right,” Sowell said. “I know how much guys are putting into it.”

As Penn State fights through the adversity, it’s been sure to look at the team as a whole for areas to correct, not pointing out individual players.

“We don't fault (Rocco). We don't fault Coach Mouser. We don't fault coach Campbell,” Sowell said. “It's all of us, and right now we're still trying to figure out how to put it all together, but the best thing that we could do is stay together.”

But how close are the Nittany Lions to actually becoming who they want to be and know they can be? Starting right tackle Anthony Donkoh thinks it should come soon, citing the bye week as a great opportunity to build upon what’s been working these last two weeks.

“We got to see what we're doing well in those moments and what is having us succeed,” Donkoh said. “Having that translate earlier to the first quarter, second quarter, third quarter for us not to be in the same situation at the end of the game, but I feel like with that, we're close in that, and it's a good thing we have this bye week to focus on that stuff and get that fixed coming for coming out the bye week.”

title: Penn State QB Rocco Becht ‘devastated’ by performance in road loss to Michigan
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Rocco Becht was in tears following Penn State’s 21-18 loss to Michigan at The Big House on Saturday night.

Becht had just thrown two interceptions and coughed up a crucial fumble. When he got back to the locker room, shielded from the 110,731 eyes looking down at him, wide receiver Chase Sowell said Becht was so distraught he wasn’t able to speak.

“He was devastated,” Sowell said. “You could see it on his face before he even got to the locker room. It killed him. The biggest thing I told him was just, keep being confident, keep being you. You don't have to make the superhero play, you just have to be Rocco Becht.”

Becht finished 28-for-44 with 267 passing yards, a touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble. All three of Michigan’s touchdowns were scored in the second half following Becht’s costly turnovers.

“I'm playing out there, I'm playing free,” Becht said. “I feel good. Some plays just aren't there for me. They just don't work out for me. I get unlucky, and that happens. It’s humbling.”

The first two turnovers were interceptions on back-to-back drives. On Penn State’s first play of the second half, Becht’s pass was picked off by safety Rod Moore, who made a diving catch along the sideline.

On the next drive, Becht had enough time in the pocket to go through his progressions and located tight end Gabe Burkle as the best target. But Becht severely underthrew the ball, and it was intercepted by cornerback Chris Bracy.

From Matt Campbell’s point of view, it was potentially Becht’s indecisiveness between whether to throw or to scramble that caused the pick.

“He came right off and said ‘I should have used my feet,’” Campbell said. “So it was a tough, tough situation, and he’ll have to continue to grow from it.”

With just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, Becht was pressured and moved out of the pocket. Instead of throwing the ball away, he held onto it and was stripped by Bracy, leading to the score which outpaced Penn State’s comeback bid.

“It’s hard to see that because it's not like he's just trying to do that,” Sowell said. “I know, obviously, he's not trying to go out there and have those plays happen, like any other guy.”

Through it all, Campbell never considered making a switch at the quarterback position. He said the same thing after Penn State’s loss to Northwestern, and he’s continued to place his trust in his starter for the last four seasons.

“Man, how that guy continues to compete and fight, and gave us a chance even at the end of the football game,” Campbell said. “He's got to be better, he will continue to grow and be better, but no, (benching him) was never a consideration from my end.”

After the game, Becht recalled Iowa State’s four-game losing skid last season and said he wasn’t expecting to have to go through a situation like that again, calling the ordeal “humbling.”

He came into his lone season at Penn State with high expectations, but the conference schedule continues to slip through his fingers. However, Becht has faith he’ll be able to bounce back from the Nittany Lions’ fourth-straight loss.

“I believe in God,” Becht said. “I’m deep in my faith, and that's what I want to continue to follow because I know there's light at the end. So, I'm going to believe in Him and trust in Him.”

title: ‘It’s paying out for him’ | Penn State WR Chase Sowell has career game despite loss to Michigan
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — When wide receiver Chase Sowell reached over a defender to haul in a 26-yard catch in the third quarter, he surpassed 100 yards on the day, proving to be Penn State’s best receiver for the second week in a row.

Sowell finished his day with 11 catches for 151 yards and a touchdown, setting career-highs in both receptions and catches in a game.

“It's just Chase has played really good football, to be quite honest with you, the last two weeks, and I'm really proud of what that guy has done,” Matt Campbell said postgame.

Sowell caught four passes on the first drive, setting the tone for the offense, and proving that last week’s outburst of 95 receiving yards was going to become a more consistent showing.

“I get that first catch or that first run, get first hit, like even if I get hit hard, it's like alright, bet,’ like now we ready, now we going,” Sowell said.

He’s not only putting the team on his back in the passing game at times, but he’s also battling through being banged up to still be his team’s most dangerous receiving threat.

After a 13-yard reception to begin the second quarter, Sowell remained down with an injury. Sowell said it was a hip drop tackle, where the defender put all his body weight onto his ankle. It didn’t keep him out of the game long, as he “was good after it,” despite the initial scare it gave him.

Sowell has filled a massive hole on offense over the past two weeks. Ever since wide receiver Koby Howard went out with an injury at the end of nonconference play, there were questions on who would step up in his absence.

It took two weeks, but Sowell has started to fill that production, getting targeted significantly more than any other Penn State receiver in Big Ten play. It stems from a mindset that Sowell has for himself when he truly gets into a rhythm.

“I would say give me the ball every time, but that's so unrealistic,” Sowell said. “I would just say it's hard to explain that it's just a mindset that you go in.”

Sowell reached double digit catches for the first time in his career, and caught his first nine passes from Rocco Becht. Any time Becht threw the ball up to him, there was a better chance of him bringing down the catch than not.

“He had a great performance out there,” running back Carson Hansen said. “He was catching whatever was thrown at him. So I love that dude, and he put so much time and effort into it. And it's paying out for him, and it was pretty cool to see him go out there and perform at a very high level.”

Sowell and Becht had a connection prior to this season at Iowa State, but even with one year already under their belt, the chemistry between the two is still growing. Sowell caught 32 passes for 500 yards at Iowa State in 2025, both numbers he’s already surpassed through seven games with the Nittany Lions.

Becht recognized that Sowell is a player who “continues to make plays when they’re out there for him to make,” and his career game against Michigan is just another instance of that.

The receiver was a big reason for Penn State’s offense continuing drives, as he tried to help the offense get back into the swing of things. In doing so, he’s given the offense more of an identity than it had prior to Week 6, becoming a true No. 1 wide receiver.

“I was just trying to find a way to kind of get the momentum going and kind of find ways to get our spark back, the swagger that I was talking about,” Sowell said. “So that was something that I was trying to feed into our offense was trying to get that swagger, trying to get some confidence back in us and get some rhythm.”

title: For Penn State women's soccer Saturday's My Game My Match reminded the team what they play for
author: Darius Harandi | For The Collegian
description:
Penn State returned to Jeffrey Field on Saturday afternoon to host Rutgers in its My Game, My Cause match, with the stands filled by families coming over for the university’s annual Family Weekend.

Looking to bounce back from a 1-0 loss at No. 13 Washington that broke a six-match unbeaten run, the Nittany Lions entered the match at 6-3-4 overall and 4-2-2 in the Big Ten.

Rutgers, at 4-5-4 and 3-4-1 in conference play, was looking to deliver Penn State its first loss at Jeffrey Field this season.

Last time the two teams faced, the blue and white won 2-1 thanks to Kaitlyn MacBean, who scored the winner in the 79th minute. Penn State led the all-time series 13-9-5, claiming victory in three of the last four meetings.

The Nittany Lions held on to an early lead, ending the match with a 1-0 victory.

Each Nittany Lion took the field representing a cause personal to her as part of Penn State’s My Game, My Cause celebration.

There was a wide variety of causes represented by the entire roster. Defender Hannah Jordan chose Best Friends Animal Society, while midfielder and captain Molly Martin represented THON, and midfielder Sophia Weixler represented Sternstunden, a charity from her home country of Germany.

For goalkeeper and captain Mackenzie Gress, the cause was deeply personal. Gress chose The V Foundation for Cancer Research.

“My (aunt) passed away almost two years ago from colon cancer, and she had an over eight-year battle with it,” Gress said.

With families packing Jeffrey Field for Family Weekend, the day carried even more significance for the blue and white.

In the opening minutes of the game, neither team was able to solidify control. Penn State found its footing first in the seventh minute when forward Ellie Kocher curled a shot 25 yards out, off the left post. The Nittany Lions recovered the rebound, feeding the ball into forward Paige Kalal, whose deflected shot sailed just over the crossbar.

After two near misses in the span of 30 seconds, the blue and white used that momentum to dominate possession and the flow of the game.

Penn State extended the pressure to the 16th minute when Kocher turned and fired a shot that deflected off a Rutgers defender, falling into the hands of Rutgers goalkeeper Olivia Bodmer. Penn State coach Erica Dambach utilized a video review to challenge the play, which uncovered that the ball had touched the defender’s arm. The subsequent penalty was converted by Kalal, giving Penn State the first goal of the match.

The goal was Kalal’s fifth of the season as well as her third successfully converted penalty kick, making her record from the spot 3-for-3.

“Being able to go up early and score and just help the team with confidence, and have that composure going into the rest of the game means a lot to me,” Kalal said.

Despite Penn State’s continued dominance, the Scarlet Knights found their first big chance in the 32nd minute through forward Lilia Calvert, Rutgers leading scorer, who curled a free-kick toward the top right corner. The shot was saved by a diving Gress.

Both teams came out of the break with noticeably more energy, creating more chances than in the first half, but neither could find the back of the net.

The match stayed even until the 75th minute, when Penn State's mentality shifted from attacking to defending. Not wanting to risk an equalizer, the Nittany Lions sat deep in their own half, conceding possession to Rutgers.

In the final minutes of the match, a desperate Rutgers attack led to a possible Penn State handball in the box. Rutgers coach Mike O’Neill used a video review, which would’ve given the Scarlet Knights a chance to tie the match. The Nittany Lions survived the late scare when the review found no penalty, and Rutgers was awarded a corner instead.

The Nittany Lions held on to their lead for the win, but to Dambach the day carried more meaning than the result.

“It’s just a chance to take a step back and realize that we’re playing a sport, we’re playing a game, and yes, it’s important, but there are much bigger, more important things in life,” Dambach said.

title: No. 15 Penn State women’s volleyball bounces back, sweeps USC on the road
author: Jimmy Blair | The Daily Collegian
description:
No. 15 Penn State looked to bounce back on Saturday night against USC after a five-set upset loss to the UCLA Bruins the previous night.

The Nittany Lions got their bounce-back win, defeating the Trojans 3-0.

Coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley ran the usual rotation that the Nittany Lions are used to putting out on the court, with Jocelyn Nathan being inserted here and there to throw off the Trojans.

Sophomore middle blocker Gabrielle Nichols got the first set started with a solo block, followed immediately by a service error from redshirt senior setter Alexis Stucky. The first set continued neck and neck, with redshirt senior outside hitter Adonia Faumuina supplying kills for the Trojans early.

A block assist followed by a kill from senior right side hitter Kennedy Martin helped the blue and white build a lead throughout the set. The Trojans responded by playing to their strength of generating blocks at the net, which they lead the Big Ten in.

The attack errors started to build up for the blue and white, inviting the Trojans back into the set. Another service error from Martin gave the Trojans a 12-11 lead.

Back-to-back kills from junior outside hitter Emmi Sellman gave the blue and white a three-point lead, and it proceeded to go up 21-14 following a run near the end of the set. A block by Nichols clinched the 25-17 first-set win for the Nittany Lions.

Penn State kept the momentum going into set two, starting with a 5-1 lead, but attack errors continued for the Nittany Lions throughout the set. Sellman and Martin kept the blue and white in the scoring column throughout the second set as USC struggled to block shots.

Outside hitter Whitney Launstein continued to be a threat for the blue and white throughout the match, along with Martin and Nichols. The Trojans had a surge, led by Faumuina, cutting Penn State’s lead down to four.

Back-to-back kills from USC redshirt junior middle blocker Leah Ford made the score 20-18 in favor of the Nittany Lions. However, this wouldn’t amount to anything for the Trojans as a kill from Launstein put Penn State in position to win the set.

Despite a comeback effort from the Trojans, a sixth kill from Martin sealed the set two victory for the blue and white.

The Fort Mill, South Carolina, native picked up right where she left off by starting the third set with two kills. However, USC wasn’t done yet, continuing to respond to any Penn State points.

An attack error by Trojans’ sophomore opposite hitter Abigail Mullen gave the blue and white an 11-7 advantage. However, Mullen answered right back with a kill. Two errors by Penn State and a block from Mia Tvrdy brought the Trojans closer.

Both sides traded blows throughout the whole set, not giving the other team an inch. Redshirt junior outside hitter London Wijay and Mullen continued to keep the Trojans in the match, while the blue and white controlled a two-point lead.

A run late kickstarted by a USC service error put the blue and white up 24-17, with plenty of cushion for match point.

Nichols ended the match with a kill assisted by Stucky, sealing the win for the Nittany Lions.

Up Next

The Nittany Lions return home Friday for a matchup against the Oregon Ducks, with start time set for 7 p.m.

title: 3 takeaways from Penn State's loss to Michigan
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Matt Campbell and Kyle Whittingham met for the first time in the Big Ten, and the first time since 2024, when Campbell’s Iowa State team beat Utah 31-28.

Penn State and Michigan played in much more of a Big Ten-style game, with the Nittany Lions falling 21-18 despite wide receiver Chase Sowell’s big game.

Here’s three takeaways from Penn State’s fourth straight loss.

Sowell only consistent receiving threat

Sowell entered the Nittany Lions’ game Saturday as probable with an injury that popped up on the availability report Thursday.

Despite the injury, Sowell proved to be a reliable receiver for Rocco Becht throughout the game. Sowell caught four passes on Penn State’s first drive, including a catch in heavy traffic.

He showed he can create separation, and even when he couldn’t, he brought in multiple contested passes to help keep drives going.

“Chase has played really good football, to be quite honest with you, the last two weeks, and you know I'm really proud of what that guy has done,” Campbell said postgame.

The only problem is that Sowell was the only consistent target for Becht.

Outside of Sowell, the most targeted receiver was tight end Andrew Rappleyea, who wasn’t featured after the second quarter until Penn State’s final drive.

Sowell finished the game with 11 catches for 151 yards and a touchdown. With Koby Howard’s return coming soon, he could have some help rather than accounting for almost half of the Nittany Lions’ receptions.

Penn State can’t finish games

After the Nittany Lions’ loss to USC in the White Out, Campbell and the players saw growth, but it wasn’t enough to finish the game, with a few crucial missed opportunities determining the outcome.

On Saturday, Penn State led 3-0 at halftime and the defense forced two interceptions from Bryce Underwood to keep Michigan off the board.

The second half was a different story, as the Wolverines’ rushing attack began to inflict its will.

Michigan capitalized off two turnovers early in the half, scoring two rushing touchdowns, compared to Penn State’s zero points off its two turnovers. Both scores came off the back of big run plays, as Bryson Kuzdzal and Savion Hiter broke runs of 43 and 41 yards, respectively, to give Michigan’s offense some life.

The Nittany Lions still had opportunities to come back, but couldn’t put anything together. The clear adjustment in Michigan’s run game during the second half wasn’t countered with adjustments in Penn State’s defense, due in part to the offense’s lack of momentum-shifting drives.

“You're right there to win the game, and you got to win in the margins right now for sure and we're not doing that,” Campbell said.

The defense dealt with the gashings in the run game and had to help the offense out, giving up 21 points in the second half. Penn State's struggles to finish games is a big reason why the Nittany Lions are winless in the conference.

Running game can't be fixed

Saturday once again featured a heavy passing attack from Penn State because the run game couldn’t put much together for the fourth straight game.

Running back Carson Hansen was the clear top option against Michigan, but the lack of consistency in his runs forced Penn State to rely on Becht’s arm.

Hansen did reach the end zone on a 2-yard rushing touchdown, but his 3.4 yards per carry on 15 rushes proved he couldn’t get any momentum going.

“We were moving the ball running-wise, but there's just some things where I'm like, ‘Man, I could be better in this area, in pass protection or whatever it is,’” Hansen said. “So yeah, there's always things that I’m like, ‘I just want one play back or two plays back.’”

The offensive line could be part of the blame for the lack of consistent running. Seven of Hansen’s carries went for two yards or less, and one of Penn State’s “most explosive guys” in running back Quinton Martin Jr., according to Taylor Mouser, didn’t even have a chance to get into the open field on either of his carries.

For the second straight game, Penn State’s longest run came from Becht on a 9-yard carry, with neither of the three backs featured having a rush over eight yards.

For a conference that features the run game so much, Penn State’s lack of ground success through the first seven games under Campbell is something that likely can’t be fully fixed before the end of the season.

title: Penn State women's soccer defeats Rutgers in a back and forth match, earns its 5th Big Ten win
author: Ava Aguiar | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions returned to Jeffrey Field on Family Weekend to take on the Scarlet Knights after a close loss against Washington last Sunday.

Penn State defeated Rutgers in a 1-0 match, keeping themselves in a good position to earn a spot in the Big Ten Tournament. The Nittany Lions currently sit at number seven, with the top eight teams qualifying.

1st half

At the start of the half, a foul on Penn State’s Bella Ayscue gave Rutgers’ Lilia Calvert a free kick opportunity. The Scarlet Knights maintained control of the ball until the sixth minute, when the Nittany Lions took back possession and had three shot attempts.

Rutgers saw its first shot opportunity after a goal kick by Olivia Bodmer was met by fellow Scarlet Knight Reilly McGlinn, but was overshot. Penn State took back possession of the ball as Aubrey Kulpa made her way into the box for a shot, but also missed.

Another shot for the Nittany Lions was just blocked by Bodmer before a handball on Rutgers’ Lindsey Hailey awarded the blue and white a penalty kick. Paige Kalal took the shot and scored to give Penn State an early lead in the 15th minute.

The Nittany Lions continued to dominate, taking the first two corners of the game before taking another two shots at goal.

Rutgers struggled to keep the blue and white out of their box, seeing no action on Mackenzie Gress in almost 10 minutes.

Both teams showed aggression with over 10 fouls being called in the first half on both sides. A foul on Penn State’s Ellie Kocher allowed the Scarlet Knights the chance to get back down the field.

After a back and forth caused more fouls, Calvert had another chance at the goal, but was blocked off the fingertips of Gress.

The Scarlet Knights ramped up their speed to match the Nittany Lions, seeing more time in the box, but failed to find an opportunity to put themselves on the board to close out the first half.

2nd Half

Both teams came into the half with fire, with Penn State taking the first corner of the half, before Rutgers took back the ball for their own corner, and saw two missed shots.

A goal kick by Gress sent the ball upfield for a shot by Kocher, but Bodmer denied it.

A foul on Kulpa left the blue and white packed into the Rutgers box for a free kick, the ball bounced around the heads of the players before Kulpa just missed the shot over the net.

An aggressive game saw multiple players down, with Gress going down before giving the okay to get back up and keep playing. However, defender Lily Boyden went down and was subbed by Lilly Burger.

“I think this was Mack's best game of the season. I thought she was outstanding and made big plays," coach Erica Dambach said. "I think she led the charge and it allowed our team to be fired up in those moments.”

The game remained a competitive back-and-forth, with both teams keeping the pressure on. Penn State maintained primary possession, but Rutgers, determined to get points on the board, kept on their heels.

The Scarlet Knights capitalized on fouls made on the blue and white, ultimately earning two free kicks, but were met each time by the Nittany Lion backline.

Ayscue moved the ball back down the field to forward Nicole Crane, before losing possession. Gress, with a powerful kick, gave it back to the blue and white offense, but losing their aggression, it was returned back to the Rutgers offense.

Rutgers took its fourth corner of the game but continued to be blocked by the defense. Olivia Robinson started to make some division between herself and the Scarlet Knights defense before being tripped and fouled.

Soon after, Rutgers’ Calvert was given a yellow card for unsporting behavior as she held down Paige Pasinski.

With a minute to go, Rutgers used its coach's challenge to look into a potential handball on Penn State. The challenge wasn't upheld, and the Nittany Lions got off with a break.

The Scarlet Knights had their final opportunity to tie up the game with another corner kick, and their seventh of the game, but it was caught on the head of a Nittany Lion.

Penn State held off any last-minute attempts from Rutgers, ending the match with a 1-0 win for its fifth Big Ten win of the season.

“I think having this win at home and getting ready to go on and play Michigan State, this is a huge momentum shifter for us, and will give us a lot of confidence going into the last few games,” Kalal said.

As the season nears its end, Dambach emphasized the need to finish strong.

“Three more games in the regular season, we got to keep taking three points. I think it honestly is so far from our minds right now, this postseason. It’s about just stacking wins and stacking this next win on Thursday night,” Dambach said.

Up Next

Penn State will travel to East Lansing to take on No. 5 Michigan State at 6 p.m. Thursday. The Spartans are currently second in the Big Ten rankings.

description:
